title: She Chose the Better Part
paragraphs:
She Chose the Better Part
The Lesson I Learned From Mary Sitting at Jesus' Feet—and Why It Changed Everything
I used to think faith was mostly about doing more.
More trying to convince God that I was serious enough, committed enough, useful enough to deserve His approval.
Then one day, I found myself exhausted.
But because I was trying to carry a relationship that God never asked me to carry alone.
That is why the story of Mary sitting at His feet hits differently the older I get.
Because if we're honest, most of us are Martha.
And very few of us are Mary.
The story is found in Luke 10:38-42.
She sits at the feet of Jesus.
Luke records it in Greek as:
Meaning she intentionally positioned herself at the Lord's feet.
In Jewish culture, sitting at someone's feet was not merely relaxation.
"You have the words I need more than anything else."
The Greek text says she was:
Literally meaning "dragged away," "pulled in different directions," or "distracted."
Service became dangerous because it pulled her away from the very Person she was serving.
How many of us know exactly what that feels like?
We move from task to task to task.
And somewhere in the chaos, Jesus becomes another item on the checklist.
But we have stopped sitting at His feet.
That is why Martha's complaint feels so relatable.
Busyness had distorted her view of Jesus.
The very Savior standing in her home was now being questioned because stress had become louder than truth.
How many believers are there today who secretly feel the same?
Lord, do You care about my marriage?
Lord, do You care about my finances?
Lord, do You care about my anxiety?
Lord, do You care about my future?
The tragedy is not that we ask those questions.
The tragedy is that we often ask them while standing only a few feet away from the One who already gave His life to answer them.
Then Jesus speaks one of the most tender corrections in all Scripture.
In Hebrew culture, repeating a name communicated affection, concern, and intimacy.
The Lord was not attacking Martha.
"You are anxious and troubled about many things."
The Greek word for anxious is:
Meaning divided, pulled apart, fragmented internally.
How many people are living there right now?
Then comes the statement that changed my life.
Not the endless demands we create for ourselves.
The phrase "good portion" carries covenant imagery.
Like finding the pearl of great price.
"It will not be taken away from her."
But what is formed in the presence of Christ cannot be stolen by circumstances.
That lesson became even clearer when I realized Mary's story does not end in Luke 10.
Jesus is only days away from the cross.
Others still do not fully understand what is coming.
She breaks open an alabaster jar worth nearly a year's wages.
Because people who spend time at the feet of Jesus often understand things that busy crowds miss.
And that is still true today.
The deepest spiritual insight rarely comes from rushing.
The Aramaic language Jesus likely spoke carried a richness often missed in modern culture.
The concept behind discipleship was never merely gathering information.
Jesus did not come merely to make us productive.
He came to make us new.
Humanity's greatest scandal was not political corruption.
Our rebellion against a holy God.
Yet Jesus stepped into our scandal.
He died the death we deserved.
Not simply to improve our lives.
But to give us entirely new ones.
That is why Mary sat at His feet.
Whether she fully understood it at that moment or not, she was sitting before the only Person who could rewrite her eternity.
For every sinner who comes to Him.
That is why our mission exists.
But to point people to the Savior who transforms scandal into grace.
If this article stirred something in your spirit, don't let it stop here.
If our desire is truly to glorify God, then supporting the work that spreads His Gospel becomes part of that worship.
Most importantly, become part of a growing community committed to biblical truth, spiritual growth, encouragement, accountability, and Gospel-centered transformation.
Or if you've been spiritually exhausted lately:
"Lord, bring me back to Your feet."
Your testimony may encourage someone else who is struggling today.
Because sometimes one honest confession opens a door for another soul to find healing.
And maybe that is why you were led to read this article all the way to the end.
Not because you needed another task.
Not because you needed another burden.
But because Jesus was reminding you of the one thing that can never be taken away.
The feet of Jesus are still the safest place in the world.
And the people who stay there are never the same.
One day every distraction will disappear, but the moments spent at His feet will echo into eternity.
The greatest tragedy is not being too busy for God—it is being so busy that you forget He was the treasure all along.
